schema_note: APPEND-ONLY pre-registered prediction ledger. Entries are NEVER edited after logging - only resolved (outcome, resolved_on, source). 'prob' is always P(claim is TRUE), so 0.5 = no idea. Directional entries must carry a non-null ref_price AND bm_ref, both stamped from the SAME price fetch at logging time and then locked; score.py refuses to grade any directional entry missing either. EXCEPTION: entries with 'basis':'absolute' are graded against their own 'threshold_pct' instead of a benchmark leg, and carry a null bm_ref - used where the subject IS the benchmark (an index-level call), since comparing the benchmark to itself would make the relative test False by construction. 'cluster' groups correlated predictions so score.py can report effective n rather than raw count. 'provenance' records which model and surface produced the entry - for attribution and reproducibility only, NOT as a model comparison (per-cell n is far too small).

predictions.resolution_note: Resolved TRUE. (a) EXISTENCE: confirmed by direct read of the primary ASX announcement 'Notice of ASIC Investigation' (DroneShield Ltd, 12 May 2026, 10:41am AEST). The complete official ASX announcement index for DRO across 2026 (through the most recent entry, 10 July 2026) contains exactly one 'ASIC' entry - the 12 May notice - with no closure, no-further-action or findings announcement since. For a listed company a closure would very likely trigger continuous disclosure, so the silence is meaningful, but it remains an inference. ERROR IN THE PRE-REGISTERED RATIONALE, LEFT UNCORRECTED: the rationale states the disclosure date as 11 May 2026; the primary source shows 12 May 2026. METHOD LESSON: this entry's resolution rule asked a source to 'confirm ... has not concluded', which is close to unsatisfiable affirmatively. Future factual rules should specify an achievable evidentiary standard (e.g. 'no closure announcement on the official record as at DATE').
